title: Public continue-link endpoint sends real email via Resend with no per-IP rate limit server-side or at the edge
evidence:
draft_handler.gleam:15-16: "////   - The continue-link endpoint always answers 200; the 10-minute
////     per-draft cooldown (claimed atomically in SQL) bounds email spam." | middleware.gleam:284-286: "    // F3 save-and-resume draft endpoints (token = auth, no session).
    [\"apply\", _, \"draft\"] -> True
    [\"apply\", _, \"continue-link\"] -> True" | csrf.gleam:97-98: same paths in should_skip | cloudflare-rate-limits.tf:58: "expression  = \"(starts_with(http.request.uri.path, \\\"/erase/\\\") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, \\\"/dsar/\\\"))\"" | worker.js:87: "const AUTH_WRITE_PATTERN = /^\/api\/v1\/(?:(?:vacancies|account|settings|notifications|payment)\b|auth\/resend-confirmation\b)/;"
detail: Paired with the unauthenticated draft-save, an attacker creates a draft for any (vacancy, victim-email) then triggers official Resend email to that victim. The 10-min cooldown is per-draft only; nothing bounds fan-out across distinct recipients (no server limiter; edge rules cover /erase//dsar/ and /api/v1/ only). Resend spend + sender-reputation risk.
recommended_fix: Add a per-IP bucket for /apply/:code/draft and /apply/:code/continue-link in the Cloudflare Worker (caches.default pattern) or a server-side per-IP throttle; keep the per-draft cooldown as second layer.
